description: Tygron is a Dutch cloud platform for spatial professionals that combines spatial data, physical models and scenario calculations in one environment so that the consequences of decisions can be seen before they are made. Users run climate, environmental and housing development scenarios for any area, test interventions, run flood and heat stress calculations and share results with stakeholders, while policy teams, engineers and authorities work in the same traceable environment. It links to the Dutch base registries BAG (buildings and addresses), AHN (elevation) and BGT (large-scale topography) as well as users' own models and workflows, without migrating their data. Tygron says the platform has been used in more than 30,000 projects by more than 100 organisations in 20 countries, from neighbourhood to provincial scale, by consultants, municipalities, provinces and water boards. Coverage: generic, with ready data links for the Netherlands. Access: software as a service; licences give full access to all computational models with unlimited runs within the licence, and extras such as square kilometres, archive space and GeoShare are priced in the platform. Licence: commercial, with published prices from 1 December 2025, indexed yearly, and GIBIT terms for municipalities. Caveats: model certification and accuracy depend on the scenario, and the counters on the home page did not render. Simulation uses: pluvial flood, heat stress and development scenarios for neighbourhoods and cities. Related records: the BAG Netherlands register, the 3D BAG and ArcGIS Urban.
